NFL DFS Quarterback Rankings: Week 6 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, October 18 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 13, 9:50 PM ET

Josh Allen is the top-projected quarterback on the Week 6 DraftKings main slate at 23.7 DraftKings points for $7,500, at Las Vegas. Matthew Stafford (22.0, $6,400) and Drake Maye (20.8, $6,600) are next.

Deshaun Watson returns the most per dollar among quarterbacks projected for at least 15 points: 3.50 projected points per $1,000 at $4,900.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 13, 9:50 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Quarterbacks to know in Week 6

Josh Allen, BUF at LV ($7,500)

Josh Allen carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 23.7 DraftKings points at $7,500, the 4th-highest on the entire main slate. That is 1.7 points clear of Matthew Stafford. The model includes 6.8 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 3.16 projected points per $1,000, 7th of 18 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Allen averaged 24.0 points with a simulated floor of 9.4 and a ceiling of 44.0, and he holds 12% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Buffalo is a 5.5-point favorite on the road against Las Vegas, with an implied team total of 29.5 in a game totaled at 53.5.

Matthew Stafford, LAR vs ARI ($6,400)

Matthew Stafford projects 2nd at the position with 22.0 DraftKings points at $6,400. The salary works out to 3.44 projected points per $1,000, 2nd of 18 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Stafford averaged 22.0 points with a simulated floor of 8.9 and a ceiling of 40.5, and he holds 19% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. The Rams are a 12.5-point favorite at home against Arizona, with an implied team total of 32 in a game totaled at 51.5.

Value: Deshaun Watson, CLE vs BAL ($4,900)

Deshaun Watson projects for 17.1 DraftKings points at $4,900, which works out to 3.50 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 18 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. The model includes 6.7 rushing attempts. Across 10,000 simulations Watson averaged 17.3 points with a simulated floor of 6.8 and a ceiling of 31.5, and he holds 5% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Cleveland is a 4.5-point underdog at home against Baltimore, with an implied team total of 18.5 in a game totaled at 41.5.
